terminal_name: Port of Koper LNG bunkering development
issue: Slovenia has zero GEM LNG terminals (confirmed, coverage-gap country). Only LNG-adjacent activity found at the Port of Koper is (a) LNG BUNKERING capability development (refueling LNG-powered ships — categorically out of scope per project definition which excludes bunkering) and (b) a June 2026 political dispute in which the Ankaran municipality alleged Luka Koper was building a 'tanker/LPG/LNG terminal,' which Luka Koper publicly denied as 'false and misleading,' stating the national spatial plan for Koper only foresees an upgrade of EXISTING capacities and explicitly does NOT foresee fixed LNG infrastructure (space/safety constraints keep any LNG support non-fixed/ship-based). No sponsor-confirmed import/export terminal project exists. Separately, Slovenia's infrastructure minister discussed importing up to 2 Qatari LNG cargoes/year via NEIGHBORING countries' terminals (Croatia's Krk FSRU, Italy's Adriatic LNG/Rovigo) — not a Slovenian facility, so out of scope for a Slovenia new_terminal.
suggested_action: No staging. Re-check Koper in a future sweep if the disputed 'gas terminal' claim resurfaces with sponsor/permit evidence, or if bunkering plans evolve into fixed marine-import infrastructure.
